title: Upper minimax value bounded by a finite row sample's lower value
statement:
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ satisfy the convex-compact minimax hypotheses for a payoff $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$, and suppose in addition that $f$ is normalized, $0 \le f(x,y) \le 1$ for all $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$. Fix an integer $M \ge 2$ and a finite row sample $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,M \to X$, writing $x_i$ for its $i$-th point. Then
\[
  \inf_{x' \in X}\; \sup_{y \in Y}\; f(x', y)
    \;\le\;
  \sup_{y \in Y}\; \inf_{i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,M}\; f(x_i, y).
\]
hypotheses_covered: convex-compact minimax hypotheses on X, Y, f
a row sample x : Fin M → X
replaced:
Under the convex-compact minimax hypotheses and the normalization $0 \le f \le 1$, for
any row sample $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,M \to X$ with $M \ge 2$,
\[
  \inf_{x' \in X} \sup_{y \in Y} f(x', y)
    \;\le\;
  \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,M} f(x_i, y).
\]
The proof constructs a finite matrix game with payoff $1 - f$ on each finite column
subset, applies the finite minimax theorem (via the upstream no-regret development), and
uses compactness of $X$ to pass to all columns.
